children: MacRitchie Investments' holding in the auto platform declined to 3.08 per cent from 6.82 per cent, while Capital Group and Norway's sovereign wealth fund bought shares worth Rs 445 crore
Singapore's state-owned investment firm Temasek has divested a 3.74 per cent stake in multi-channel automobile platform CarTrade Tech for Rs 470.10 crore through an open market transaction.

Temasek, through its affiliate MacRitchie Investments Pte Ltd, sold 18.20 lakh shares of Navi Mumbai-based CarTrade Tech at an average price of Rs 2,583 apiece, according to bulk deal data available on the BSE on Friday.
Following the transaction, MacRitchie Investments' holding in CarTrade Tech declined to 3.08 per cent from 6.82 per cent.
Capital Group, Norway Fund Buy Shares

On the buying side, US-based Capital Group, through its arm SmallCap World Fund Inc, and Norway's Government Pension Fund Global jointly acquired more than 17.23 lakh shares, representing a 3.54 per cent stake in CarTrade Tech.
The shares were purchased at an average price of Rs 2,583 apiece, taking the combined transaction value to approximately Rs 445 crore.
Shares of CarTrade Tech rose 3.72 per cent to close at Rs 2,699.30 apiece on the BSE on Friday.
